PLD.name: Prologis
PLD.numbers_line: Core FFO $1.60 a share ($1.61 ex promotes); FMP shows EPS $1.60 vs a $0.78 estimate, but that estimate is a GAAP-EPS figure so the 'beat' is not like for like; revenue $2.39B vs $2.18B est. Occupancy 95.6%, rent change on rollover 38% net effective (23% cash), same-store NOI +5.7% (5.9% cash).
PLD.guidance: Core FFO $6.25–6.29 for the year; same-store NOI raised to 5.5–6% net effective and 7–7.5% cash; development starts raised to $6–6.75B (a very large Q4 of build-to-suits, 55–65% of the year's starts); acquisitions raised to $2.1–2.3B; dispositions and contributions trimmed to $3.5–4.75B and strategic-capital revenue to $650–660M on caution about pricing; average occupancy 95.25–95.5%. SEGRO closes in H1 2027 and will not be in initial 2027 guidance.
call_said: The rate shock, named plainly: 'the abrupt shift in the interest rate environment', a wider bid-ask spread, transaction volumes to moderate, 'some pressure on values', and the bar for allocating capital 'raised even further'. Offset: replacement-cost rents are now 27% above market, so new supply does not pencil and starts should fall. 95% of debt is fixed with ~8 years of life; $9B of liquidity.

Data centres: a 5.8 GW pipeline (1.7 GW with secured power, 4.1 GW advanced), letters of intent on ~1 GW mostly starting in 2027, over $2B of data-centre starts this year, unaffected by moratoriums. Separately, the data-centre supply chain is now 17% of US new logistics leasing and an estimated 150M sq ft of demand through 2030.

The logistics recovery is broadening: US net absorption 63M sq ft (a ~240M annual pace), vacancy down to 7.1%, market rents up a third straight quarter, Dallas, Houston, Atlanta, Phoenix on pace for 5–6% rent growth; Southern California recovering, South Bay aerospace 'a renaissance'. Interest-rate-sensitive tenants are 'a little bit slower'.
PLD.quote: "Our bar for allocating capital was already high, and in response, we've raised it even further." — Dan Letter
PLD.read_through: Real estate is where the rate move bites first, and even the best-capitalised landlord is flagging values and pulling in; the saving grace is the data-centre build-out carrying leasing. Read for CCI (21 Oct), DLR (22 Oct), AMT (27 Oct) and the REIT tape generally.

PNC.name: PNC Financial
PNC.numbers_line: Adjusted EPS $5.09 vs $4.91 est (beat); revenue $6.56B vs $6.61B est (light); ROTCE above 18%; NII $4.2B (+2% q/q), NIM 2.94% (−2bp); CET1 9.8%.
PNC.guidance: 2026: average loans +13.5%, NII +15.5%, fees +10.5%, revenue +13.7%, expense +9.5%. Q4 vs Q3: loans +2.5%, NII +4%, fees +3.5% with capital-markets fees up ~15%, expense +5%, charge-offs ~$250M; NIM calculated at 3% or above in Q4. 2027: management 'would agree with' the consensus of $1.0–1.1B of NII growth. Buybacks ~$560M again in Q4. Macro: Fed hikes in December and March to 4.25–4.5%, GDP above 2%.
call_said: Loan growth is the story and half of it landed in the last two weeks of the quarter: $47B added year to date (+14%), $30B of it organic, expansion markets growing 2–3× legacy and now bigger than legacy in corporate banking, ~500 new C&IB clients, capital-markets fees +40% year to date. The growth is high-quality, low-spread paper that 'constrains NIM' but pays in fees. 'Higher rates… is going to crimp CapEx', but 'we're not seeing any instance of that yet'.

Demchak on AI agents moving money: 'incredibly unsafe', 'not going to happen on my watch' without liability law, authentication and a human in the loop. PNC has quietly built the infrastructure for an 'agentic workforce' (GPUs in its own data centres, one data lake, agent-aware HR and access control) and will 'show up when we have something positive to show you'. A large acquisition would 'destroy massive value' by slowing that.

Credit: non-performers +8% on already-reserved CRE office pull-through plus one service-provider credit; delinquencies down to 0.34%; Basel III endgame worth about a point of CET1. Asked how much growth is AI capex: unknowable directly, but 'if the CapEx broadly slows down related to AI… would it slow our loan growth? Yes.'
PNC.quote: "The clouds are as dark as they ever were, but economy still strong and people are investing into it." — Bill Demchak
PNC.read_through: Commercial credit demand is real and broad at a super-regional, with the admitted dependence on the AI capex cycle for the knock-on. Same two hikes by March that JPM and BAC assume; same 'not yet' on rate damage.

SCHW.name: Charles Schwab
SCHW.numbers_line: Adjusted EPS $1.69 vs $1.65 est (beat, +29% y/y); revenue $7.17B vs $7.18B est (in line, a record); core net new assets $190B (+38%), 10.7M daily trades, margin balances $187.9B, bank loans $72.3B (+35%), sweep cash $492.8B.
SCHW.guidance: Full-year revenue growth and NIM expansion toward the lower end of the summer ranges, expenses at the low end, ~800bp of positive operating leverage (double what was expected in January). Q4 NIM up 25–30bp year over year and expanding again in 2027; a detailed 2027 scenario in January; mid-teens EPS growth through the cycle.
call_said: AI, concretely: Schwab blocks unauthorised agents logging in for clients (a daily report, 'not many'), launches 'Charlie', is the first RIA custodian in Claude for Financial Advisors, and lets clients' LLMs connect to its MCP servers with no money movement; clients trading through LLMs and APIs doubled in six months and hold more cash, not less. Developer productivity +25%.

Cash: the September dip was clients buying stocks and IPOs, 'not cash sorting in any way'; ~$190B of sub-2% securities still to roll into loans or higher yields; lending balances now exceed the securities book. Rates sensitivity unchanged at $250–300M per 25bp.

The tax-aware long-short programme grew faster than planned when a competitor ran out of capacity, so Schwab raised minimums in mid-September to throttle it, with no slowdown in advisor net new assets; a proprietary long-short product is coming. Prediction markets on financial events and company KPIs (with Cboe) over 12–18 months, no sports; crypto transfers and three new coins by year-end; after-hours trading is 1–2% of activity.
SCHW.quote: "The more people use AI, the more cash they hold because they are more active in buying stocks." — Rick Wurster
SCHW.read_through: Retail is fully engaged: record trades, record margin, record flows, cash going into the market. That is the sentiment read for the whole universe, and the prediction-markets and crypto lines are the HOOD (27 Oct) and COIN read.

TSM.name: Taiwan Semiconductor (ADR)
TSM.numbers_line: FMP (ADR): EPS $4.60 vs $4.45 est (beat), revenue $46.06B vs $45.67B est. Company: revenue $46.7B, +16.2% q/q and above the high end of guidance; gross margin 66.4% (−130bp on the 2nm ramp), operating margin 58.7%, ROE 45.5%; HPC 68% of revenue (+22% q/q), 2nm already 8% of wafer revenue.
TSM.guidance: Q4 revenue $52.3–54.3B (+14% q/q, +58% y/y at the midpoint), gross margin 65–67%, operating margin 56.5–58.5%. Full-year 2026 growth raised to ~44% in US dollars. Capex $60–64B reiterated; 2026–28 capex 'even more significantly higher' than the past three years. Overseas-fab dilution widens to 3–4 points in the back half of the five-year window. The AI-accelerator growth rate (mid-to-high 50s a year to 2029) 'probably will be higher'.
call_said: Wei: demand is 'extremely robust… we did not see any sign of slowdown' and the gap to supply 'is still quite big'. TSMC now sends its own teams to check US data-centre construction and power ('so far so good'). The one caution: consumer and price-sensitive segments 'are being challenged' by rising component prices, so planning into 2027 is 'prudent'.

Capacity at an 'unprecedented pace': ~20 fabs in progress (13 in Taiwan, 5–6 overseas); N2 capacity more than doubles in 2027; A14 risk production 2027, volume 2028, and 'a bigger node than N2'; three new 3nm fabs including Arizona fab 2 in Q3 2027 (ahead of plan) and a new Tainan fab in H1 2028; Texas is being evaluated and TSMC is in talks to run capacity at a customer's 'Terafab'. A GlobalFoundries interposer deal addresses a back-end shortage; 5× reticle advanced packaging is in production, 9× and 14× in development, and TSMC hinted it would back up customers if Intel's EMIB-T falls short.

Pricing is 'very strategic' by segment, node and location, with US-made wafers priced differently; no subletting of allocated capacity (mask-licensing only, tiny). High-NA EUV in 2030 is a maturity-and-cost choice, not a disadvantage. Agentic-AI CPUs are a rising demand line but stay outside the AI-accelerator definition.
TSM.quote: "We have no intention to leave food on the table for others." — C.C. Wei
TSM.read_through: This is the chip pack's supply-side truth: 44% growth, capex going up again, N2 doubling, and the customer is still short. Capacity-bound demand for NVDA, AVGO, AMD and the HBM makers (MU) through 2027; the consumer warning is the read for AAPL, QCOM and DELL; the Texas/Terafab line is the TSLA and SpaceX angle.

USB.name: U.S. Bancorp
USB.numbers_line: EPS $1.34 vs $1.32 est (beat, +10% y/y, ~$0.07 of reserve build); revenue $7.97B vs $8.00B est (a record ~$8B, +8.7%); NIM 2.84% (+5bp); 240bp of positive operating leverage (440bp ex BTIG); CET1 10.8%.
USB.guidance: Q4 year over year: NII +6–7%, fees +13–14% (half from BTIG), expense +8% (~4% ex BTIG). Full year revenue growth raised to 8–9% (6–7% ex BTIG, was 5–7%); operating leverage ~300bp (400bp ex BTIG, was 200/300). NIM up a similar ~5bp in Q4 with a path to 3% in 2027; ~$10B a quarter of fixed assets reprice at ~+125bp; deposit beta ~50% to start. Buybacks, paused in Q3, resume 'over the next quarter or two' toward a 70–75% payout, without counting on Basel III.
call_said: Why the buyback paused: strong loan growth, the Amazon small-business card book ($1.7B at period end), and a 40bp AOCI hit from the rate and spread move; CET1 ex-AOCI 9.1%, TCE 6.6%. Capital will 'build from here' at ~30bp a quarter.

Capital markets to go from 8% to 10%-plus of revenue over 3–5 years with BTIG ($226M of fees this quarter); corporate payments +19% with a fuel-price tailwind in fleet and freight; a USBDC stablecoin pilot launched for which 'there is not much client demand at all. What there is now is client curiosity.'

Credit and demand: C&I flat sequentially because non-bank-financial balances ran off and some deals 'did not hurdle', but pipelines 'robust' in food and beverage, energy, technology and SBA lending; CRE and residential mortgage 'muted'; card FICOs improving as balances grow; consumer spend high. No AI cash-sorting agents seen interacting with the bank.
USB.quote: "There is not much client demand at all. What there is now is client curiosity." — Gunjan Kedia, on the stablecoin pilot
USB.read_through: Same picture as the money-centres from a super-regional: broad commercial demand, clean consumer credit, NIM rising on repricing, and the rate shock on AOCI as the thing that paused capital return. The stablecoin candour is a useful counterweight to the tokenisation enthusiasm elsewhere.
